title: ISMIP7 Antarctic Observational Datasets
description: A curated collection of third-party Antarctic observational datasets assembled for the ISMIP7 ice-sheet modelling protocol (the "Observational MIPkit"), comprising a merged NetCDF of bed/surface topography, ice masks, thickness-change rates, geothermal heat flux, and surface velocity on a common 500 m polar-stereographic grid, plus regridded ocean topography and drainage basins, a Southern Ocean hydrographic climatology, and glacier calving-front, velocity, and cliff-height observations.
readme:
## data__README.md # ISMIP7 Antarctic observational datasets Observational datasets collected for the ISMIP7 Antarctic experiments, provided as a convenience for ice-sheet modellers rather than as part of the ISMIP7 protocol. This is the collection the protocol refers to as the **Observational MIPkit**. Nothing here is required: modellers are free to initialise and calibrate from other data. Everything in this collection is third-party. **Each dataset carries its own licence and citation**, given in the `README.md` of its directory and summarised here. Licence texts are in [`LICENSES/`](LICENSES/). | Directory | Contents | Licence | | --- | --- | --- | | `mipkit/` | `AntarcticaObsISMIP7-v1.2.nc` — the ISMIP7 observations MIPkit: topography and masks (BedMachine, Bedmap3), ice-presence mask, thickness-change rates, geothermal heat flux, surface velocity mosaics and time series, and drainage basins, on a common 500 m polar-stereographic grid | Compiled by the ISMIP7 observations group, who state no restrictions on access or use; each component has its own citation — see the directory README | | `ocean/topography/` | Bedmap3 and BedMachine Antarctica v3 regridded to the ISMIP7 8 km ocean grid | Bedmap3: CC-BY-4.0. BedMachine: no restrictions on access or use | | `ocean/IMBIE-basins/` | IMBIE drainage basins on the ISMIP7 8 km ocean grid, from the MEaSUREs Antarctic Boundaries dataset | NASA MEaSUREs product, no licence stated; cite Mouginot et al. (2017) | | `ocean/climatology/zhou_annual_06_nov/` | The OCEAN ICE Southern Ocean climatology (Zhou et al.) on the ISMIP7 8 km / 60 m grid — the reference the ISMIP7 AIS ocean forcing is bias-corrected to | CC-BY-4.0 | | `calving/` | Ice-front positions, velocities and cliff heights for four glaciers with tall calving cliffs, from a manuscript in review — see `calving/README.md` by its authors | The authors have not yet attached a licence; please contact them before reuse beyond ISMIP7 | ## Citing Cite the original dataset for anything you use, as given in each directory's README. The observations MIPkit itself will receive a DOI and a publication; until then, see the ISMIP7 observations focus group page for the current guidance on citing and acknowledging it: https://www.ismip.org/participants/focus-groups/observations ## Licences - `LICENSES/CC-BY-4.0.txt` — Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International, https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/ ## Contact ISMIP7 observations focus group, via the ISMIP discussion board: https://github.com/orgs/ismip/discussions ## data__calving__README.md # High-end calving calibration data The files provided contain part of the dataset generated for the submitted manuscript, “Empirical constraints on ice-cliff calving.” [(preprint)](https://doi.org/10.21203/rs.3.rs-7133627/v1). The dataset includes ice front positions, velocities, and cliff heights for four glaciers where we observed ice cliff heights above 90 m using ICESat-2 and that undergo ice-front retreat from 2019-2023. ## Dataset context These observations include four glaciers where the calving of tall cliffs resulted in rapid but short-lived retreat. Eventually, all cliffs subsequently advanced, during which dynamic thinning either rapidly reduced the cliff height, or the cliffs re-advanced with little/no change in height. Contrary to existing parameterizations of MICI, calving rates did not always monotonically increase with cliff height, even after very tall cliffs formed and retreat into thicker ice occurred. Nonetheless, the data should be useful to calibrate calving rates in locations where tall cliffs retreat rapidly. ### Glaciers Frost Glacier, East Antarctica
Fleming Glacier, Antarctic Peninsula
Commandant Charcot Glacier, East Antarctica
Tuttulikassaap Sermia (Hayes Glacier), Greenland
## Variables ### ice_fronts Each folder (labeled by glacier name) contains a shapefile of the ice front positions over the survey period. Each shapefile contains two columns: 'id': the date of the ice front trace in YYYYMMDD
'geometry': a linestring of the ice front in x,y polar stereographic coordinates (EPSG 3031/3413) ### velocities Each folder (labeled by glacier name) contains netcdf files with velocity data generated using auto-RIFT (Gardner et al., 2018) and provided by the NASA MEaSUREs ITS_LIVE project, cropped to the glacier area. 'v': mean annual velocity (m/y)
'x': x-coordinate (EPSG 3031/3413)
'y': y-coordinate (EPSG 3031/3413)
### cliff_heights This folder contains a .csv file for each glacier. Ice cliff coordinates and heights were collected by ICESat-2 and are therefore point (not gridded) data. 'x': x-coordinate of ice cliff (EPSG 3031/3413)
'y': y-coordinate of ice cliff(EPSG 3031/3413)
'cliff_height': elevation of ice cliff above the waterline (m)
'date': date of ice cliff measurement (YYYY-MM-DD) ## data__mipkit__README.md # ISMIP7 observations MIPkit for Antarctica `AntarcticaObsISMIP7-v1.2.nc` (v1.2, 12 May 2026), compiled by Mathieu Morlighem on behalf of the ISMIP7 observations group. One file, 500 m polar-stereographic grid (EPSG:3031), with the sources below recorded in each variable's `source` attribute. The file states `license: No restrictions on access or use`. It will receive a DOI and be presented in a publication; for the current guidance on citing or acknowledging it, see https://www.ismip.org/participants/focus-groups/observations. Please also cite the original dataset for each variable you use. ## Contents and sources | Variables | Source | | --- | --- | | `mask_bedmachine`, `surface_bedmachine`, `thickness_bedmachine`, `bed_bedmachine` | BedMachine Antarctica v4.1 (Morlighem et al., 2020) | | `mask_bedmap3`, `surface_bedmap3`, `thickness_bedmap3`, `bed_bedmap3` | Bedmap3 (Pritchard et al., 2025) — CC-BY-4.0 | | `icemask_greene` | Ice-presence mask, Greene et al. (2022) | | `dhdt_smith` | Thickness change from ICESat and ICESat-2, Smith et al. (2020) | | `dhdt_cpom` | Thickness change from radar altimetry (ERS-1, ERS-2, Envisat, CryoSat-2, Sentinel-3A/B), CPOM | | `geothermal_heat_flux1` | Stål et al. (2021) | | `geothermal_heat_flux2` | Lösing and Ebbing (2021) | | `vx_mosaic`, `vy_mosaic` | MEaSUREs InSAR-based Antarctica ice velocity map, version 2 (Rignot et al., 2017) | | `vx_timeseries`, `vy_timeseries` | Annual velocity time series (source not recorded in the file) | | `mouginot_basins` | Drainage basins of Mouginot et al. (2017), extrapolated | | `geoid` | EIGEN-6C4 geoid minus WGS84 ellipsoid | ## Citations - Morlighem, M. et al. (2020). NASA National Snow and Ice Data Center Distributed Active Archive Center. https://doi.org/10.5067/AXE4121732AD ## data__ocean__IMBIE-basins__README.md # IMBIE drainage basins on the ISMIP7 8 km ocean grid `IMBIE-basins_AIS_obs_ocean_v3.nc`: the IMBIE Antarctic drainage basins from the MEaSUREs Antarctic Boundaries dataset of Mouginot, Scheuchl and Rignot, rasterised onto the ISMIP7 8 km grid by the ISMIP7 AIS ocean focus group. The same basins on the other ISMIP7 grids are in the melt-calibration collection (`imbie2/`). ## Licence NASA MEaSUREs product. The data are freely available; the provider states no licence. Please cite: - Mouginot, J., Scheuchl, B. and Rignot, E. (2017). MEaSUREs Antarctic Boundaries for IPY 2007–2009 from Satellite Radar, Version 2 [Data set]. NASA National Snow and Ice Data Center Distributed Active Archive Center. https://doi.org/10.5067/AXE4121732AD ## data__ocean__climatology__zhou_annual_06_nov__README.md # OCEAN ICE Southern Ocean climatology on the ISMIP7 grid Annual climatology (1972–2024) of practical salinity (`so/`), thermal forcing (`tf/`) and potential temperature (`thetao/`) from the OCEAN ICE Southern Ocean Climatology of Zhou et al., regridded to the ISMIP7 8 km / 60 m grid and extrapolated under the ice shelves by the ISMIP7 AIS ocean focus group. This is the climatology the ISMIP7 AIS ocean forcing is bias-corrected to (reference period 1995–2024). ## Licence CC-BY-4.0 (Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International), as attached to the source datasets on SEANOE. The licence text is in `LICENSES/CC-BY-4.0.txt` at the top of the `obs/` collection. ## Citations - Zhou, S., Dutrieux, P. and Giulivi, C. (2024). The OCEAN ICE Southern Ocean Climatology [Data set]. SEANOE. https://doi.org/10.17882/103946 - Zhou, S., Dutrieux, P., Giulivi, C., Lee, W. S., Kim, T.-W., Hattermann, T. and Janout, M. (2026). Southern Ocean (90°S–45°S) conservative temperature and absolute salinity profiles compilation (OCEAN ICE D1.1) [Data set]. SEANOE. https://doi.org/10.17882/99787 - Zhou, S., Dutrieux, P., Giulivi, C., Meijers, A., Lee, W. S., Kim, T.-W., Hattermann, T. and Janout, M. (2026). The OCEAN ICE hydrography profiles compilation and climatology. *Earth System Science Data Discussions* [preprint], in review. https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-2025-727 ## data__ocean__topography__README.md # Topography on the ISMIP7 8 km ocean grid Bedmap3 and BedMachine Antarctica v3, conservatively regridded to the ISMIP7 8 km grid by the ISMIP7 AIS ocean focus group, with floating and grounded fractions per cell. Each file keeps the global attributes of its source. ## Licences and citations **`bedmap3/bedmap3_AIS_obs_ocean_topography_v3.nc`** — CC-BY-4.0 (Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International), as stated by the UK Polar Data Centre.
